land.text: Najd, where the Al Saud returned in 1824 'after the fall of the First Saudi state in 1818'

predecessors.note: Six years separate the two states; Najd was held by Ottoman-Egyptian forces in between (the Nejd page: Turki 'retook Riyadh from Ottoman-Egyptian forces').

land.text: Riyadh, retaken from the Ottoman-Egyptian forces in 1824

predecessors.note: The Egyptian garrison of Riyadh is the counterpart of the founding event.

land.text: Riyadh, Najd and Qassim, taken by the Rashidis of Ha'il after the Battle of Mulayda (21 January 1891)

successors.note: The Al Saud returned to Riyadh in January 1902 as a new state, the Third Saudi State (third-saudi-state), taking Riyadh back from the Rashidis.

capitals.name: Riyadh
capitals.note: The text says Turki 'made his capital in Riyadh'. The page's infobox lists capital years 1824-1834 and 1889-1891 but the extract lost the names; no other seat is named on the pages opened (a gap-filler should read the infobox).

keyframe_review.note: 5,522 km2 for 1824 (a disc of about 42 km around Riyadh): 'Turki bin Abdullah retook Riyadh from Ottoman-Egyptian forces' in 1824 and made it his capital. The page gives no area to compare with; the shape is the city and its oasis, which is what the page supports.

375,679 km2: Riyadh province and Qassim. The Expedition page: Turki 'captured Riyadh, Arid, Kharj, Mahmal, Sudayr and Aflaj' and had 'minimal control over Qasim and Ha'il' even by 1830, so the Qassim part of the shape is a soft, nominal claim. The page dates none of the captures; Cliopatria's 1825 start is kept (confidence 1 in the ledger).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1828 shape without the Ha'il province, where Saudi control was 'minimal'

keyframe_review.note: 490,704 km2: this shape adds the whole Ha'il province, but by 1830 Turki 'had minimal control over Qasim and Ha'il' and Ha'il became a Rashidi vassal emirate only in 1836 (Jabal Shammar page). The correction removes Ha'il; the corrected shape is within 1% of the 1825 shape, so the 1828 growth is Cliopatria's Ha'il addition and nothing more.

correction.text: Najd, Qassim and Hasa without Ha'il; hatched while Muhammad Ali's army held it, 1837-1840

keyframe_review.note: 563,108 km2 for 1830-1845. Hasa is added in 1830 ('By 1830 he was able to assert his authority over Hasa'), which the shape shows, but it also keeps Ha'il (see 1828) and ignores the Egyptian occupation of Najd, al-Hasa and Qatif in 1837-1840 (ledger: occupation_start 1837, occupation_end April 1840). The correction removes Ha'il for 1830-1845; the Ha'il emirate is a Saudi vassal 1836-1848.

correction.text: Najd, Qassim and Hasa without sovereign Ha'il

keyframe_review.note: 532,312 km2 for 1846-1852. Ha'il stays inside the shape although the Jabal Shammar infobox gives 'Sovereign kingdom (1848-1921)' after 'Nominal vassal of the Second Saudi State (1836-1848)'. The correction removes Ha'il.

correction.text: Najd, Qassim, Hasa and the desert south and east of them, without the Gulf coast, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait and Ha'il

keyframe_review.note: 1,116,421 km2, Cliopatria's maximum. The shape reaches the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and the edge of Oman, but the pages say otherwise: Faisal 'unsuccessfully attempted to capture Oman and Bahrain' in the 1850s, held Qatar only for weeks in 1851, and 'attacked the Trucial States in the 1860s' until 'the British forces militarily stopped his attacks'; Bahrain and Muscat paid him tribute, which is not territory. The correction removes the Trucial Coast, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait and Ha'il (sovereign since 1848); what is left, about 0.94 M km2, still doubles the 1852 shape and the pages do not date or explain the addition (ledger, confidence 1). No infobox area exists on the page.

correction.text: the 1856 outline without the Gulf coast, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait and Ha'il

keyframe_review.note: 1,038,353 km2 for 1856-1865, Faisal's last decade; same fault as 1853 (Qatar, the Trucial coast and Kuwait fringes inside the shape, Ha'il a sovereign neighbour). Same correction.

correction.text: the 1866 outline without the Gulf coast, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait and Ha'il

keyframe_review.note: 816,945 km2 for 1866-1872. Holds for 1866-1870 after removing the same fringes. The Ottomans took al-Hasa in 1871 ('conquered al-Hasa from an Ottoman garrison which had controlled the area from 1871', Unification page), so 1871-1872 is the new keyframe emirate-of-nejd_1871.

minus.text: the 1866 outline without the Gulf coast, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait and Ha'il

correction.text: the 1866 outline without al-Hasa and Qatif, held by the Ottomans from 1871

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1871-1872: the 1866 outline without al-Hasa, taken by the Ottomans in 1871 while Abdullah and Saud fought for the imamate (Saud 'proclaimed himself Imam in May 1871').

375,513 km2 for 1873-1876: Najd and Qassim, as Saud 'gained power again in 1873' and held it to 1875. The cut from the 1866 shape is Hasa (1871) plus about 730 cells of southern desert that no page mentions (ledger 1873, confidence 1).

324,040 km2 for 1877-1879: Qassim shrinks to 29% of the province, passing to the Rashidis' shape. The Jabal Shammar page says the Rashidis and the Saudis 'engaged into a full scale war over the region of Qassim' but dates nothing; the Unification page has the Saudis winning Qassim back on 13 April 1906. Unverified: page budget.
324,206 km2 for 1880-1884: the 1877 shape again (a few cells added). Unverified: page budget; no page dates a change in these years.

correction.text: unchanged outline, 1885-1886 free and 1887-1889 hatched as land the Rashidis annexed

keyframe_review.note: 268,433 km2 for 1885-1889. The Muhammad bin Abdullah page: 'In 1887 he annexed Najd', captured Riyadh and appointed a Rashidi governor (Salim Al Sibhan) 'rather than restoring Abdullah bin Faisal'. The shape is kept (the remnant still carried the Saudi name, and the infobox gives capital years 1889-1891) but is hatched, Rashidi-held, from 1887 (ledger occupation_start 1887).

correction.text: unchanged outline, years 1890 to 21 January 1891 only

keyframe_review.note: 114,136 km2 for 1890-1894. The Battle of Mulayda 'occurred on 21 January 1891' and was the 'End of the Second Saudi State': the shape holds for 1890 and the first weeks of 1891 only, then passes to Jabal Shammar (dissolve event). The 1891-1894 years belong to the Rashidis.

correction.text: not a Saudi shape: no Saudi state exists 1892-1901

keyframe_review.note: 52.5 km2 for 1895-1904 near Ha'il (40.6 E, 28.8 N), an artefact (data/README lists it as a tiny shape). The Al Saud had no state between the defeat of Mulayda (January 1891) and the retaking of Riyadh on 13 January 1902 (Emirate of Riyadh page); Abdul Rahman bin Faisal was expelled from Najd in 1891. Drop the shape; the land belongs to emirate-of-jabal-shammar until 1902.

region.text: Riyadh and its oasis, retaken from the Ottoman-Egyptian forces

ledger.note: 1824: Turki bin Abdullah retakes Riyadh and founds the Second Saudi State. Page (closely paraphrased): Turki 'retook Riyadh from Ottoman-Egyptian forces', 'after the fall of the First Saudi state in 1818', and made it his capital.

region.text: Riyadh, Arid, Kharj, Mahmal, Sudayr and Aflaj

ledger.note: 1825: Turki's authority spreads over the Riyadh province. Page: he 'captured Riyadh, Arid, Kharj, Mahmal, Sudayr and Aflaj'; the page dates none of them, so 1825 is Cliopatria's year for the first large shape (page silent).

region.text: Hasa

ledger.note: 1830: Hasa comes under Najd. Page: 'By 1830 he was able to assert his authority over Hasa but had minimal control over Qasim and Ha'il'; the Faisal page has Faisal 'sent on military operations to Al Hasa in the east' in 1830. The year is the page's 'by 1830'; the previous holder is not named.

region.text: Ha'il, governed by Abdullah bin Rashid as Faisal's appointee

ledger.note: 1836: Ha'il becomes a Saudi vassal emirate under Abdullah bin Rashid. Page: 'The Emirate of Jabal Shammar was established in 1836 as a vassal of the second Saudi state'; infobox 'Nominal vassal of the Second Saudi State (1836-1848)'. The Faisal page says Faisal appointed Abdullah Amir of Ha'il in 1835.

minus.text: the Ha'il province, the Rashidi vassal emirate of the Saudi state from 1836 (ledger 3)

region.text: Najd, al-Hasa and Qatif, 'occupied' by Mehmet Ali, without the Ha'il province

ledger.note: 1837: Muhammad Ali's army occupies Najd. Page: 'Mehmet Ali's forces landed at Yanbu in 1836 and marched against Najd', 'Khalid entered Riyadh in 1837', 'Mehmet Ali had occupied Najd, al-Hasa and Qatif'; in 1838 Hurshid Pasha 'defeated' Faisal, who was taken captive to Cairo. The year is the page's; the extent is the page's three names. fx-37: the Ha'il province (453 cells of the gazetteer's Nejd) is subtracted: the page names 'Najd, al-Hasa and Qatif' and puts Ha'il only in Turki's 'minimal control over Qasim and Ha'il'; it never says the Egyptians occupied it, and the Jabal Shammar vassal relation (ledger 3) holds Ha'il until 1848. The Muhammad Ali dossier's own gains of 1838 and loss of 1841 already leave Ha'il out.

minus.text: the Ha'il province, the Rashidi vassal emirate of the Saudi state from 1836 (ledger 3)

region.text: Najd, al-Hasa and Qatif, evacuated by the Egyptian army, without the Ha'il province

ledger.note: April 1840: the Egyptian army is recalled from Najd. Page: 'European pressure and British diplomacy led to the recall of most of the army from Najd and eastern Arabia in April 1840'; the Nejd page: after the Convention of London 'the Ottoman Empire withdrew their military presence in the Arabian Peninsula'. The Egyptian-backed Khalid bin Saud was toppled soon afterwards by Abdullah bin Thunayan and 'the rule over Najd ended by the close of 1841'. fx-37: the Ha'il province is subtracted, as in ledger 4, so that the end closes the same land.

region.text: Najd and Hasa under nominal Ottoman suzerainty

ledger.note: 1843: Faisal returns to Riyadh and recognises Ottoman suzerainty. Page: he 'reclaimed the throne in 1843', 'recognised the supremacy of the Ottoman Empire in the region' and the Ottomans 'appointed him governor of Najd'; the Nejd page adds an annual tribute. The year is the return's; the recognition is undated and nominal in practice (Faisal governed alone).

region.text: the Bahrain islands, tributary

ledger.note: 1847: Bahrain pays tribute to Faisal. Page: 'In 1847, he attempted to intervene in Bahrain', failed to take it and 'accepted a peace deal that included tribute'; the page lists tribute from Bahrain among his income. The page does not say who paid whom in so many words; the reading is that Bahrain's Al Khalifa paid.

region.text: Ha'il, now sovereign under Abdullah bin Rashid

ledger.note: 1848: Ha'il becomes sovereign. Page infobox: 'Nominal vassal of the Second Saudi State (1836-1848) Sovereign kingdom (1848-1921)'. Faisal and the Rashidis stayed allied (a daughter of Faisal married Abdullah bin Rashid).

region.text: Qatar, held for weeks

ledger.note: June 1851: Faisal takes Qatar after Mesaimeer. Page: 'After the Battle of Mesaimeer' (2-4 June 1851) Faisal 'gained temporary control of Qatar, which had been under Bahraini control'; Mohammed bin Thani sent a letter 'agreeing to be his subject' (Faisal page).

region.text: Qatar, returned after the 25 July agreement

ledger.note: 25 July 1851: the peace of Mesaimeer. Page: the agreement brokered by Saeed bin Tahnun Al Nahyan 'required Ali bin Khalifa to pay 4,000 German krones yearly as zakat, and required Faisal to return Al Bidda Fort' and stop interfering in Qatar.

region.text: the land Cliopatria adds in 1853 beyond the 1846 outline, page silent

ledger.note: 1853: Cliopatria's shape doubles. The pages give no date or place for the addition (the Eastern Province coast and the sand desert); the Faisal page only says Faisal 'targeted Al-Ahsa, Qatif, and Saihat' for revenue. Recorded at confidence 1 as the difference between the corrected 1853 and 1846 outlines.

region.text: the Bahrain islands

ledger.note: 1865: Bahrain's tribute lapses with Faisal's death. Page: 'After Faisal's death in 1865, the state declined amid succession fights between his sons'; the page does not mention the tribute again, so the end is a bridge.

minus.text: the 1866 outline without the Gulf coast, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait and Ha'il

region.text: the north-western and southern fringes Cliopatria's 1866 outline drops, page silent

ledger.note: 1866: the outer desert falls away. After Faisal's death 'Abdullah became Imam, but was immediately challenged by the ambitious Saud'; the first fighting was at Mutala in 1866-67. Cliopatria's 1866 shape is about 100,000 km2 smaller than the 1865 one; no page names what was lost, so this is a bridge.

region.text: al-Hasa and Qatif

ledger.note: 1871: the Ottomans take al-Hasa. Page: the Saudis 'conquered al-Hasa from an Ottoman garrison which had controlled the area from 1871'; the Saud page says Midhat Pasha 'took advantage of the opportunity to sweep into the province of Al Hasa' during the Abdullah-Saud war.

minus.text: the 1866 outline without the Gulf coast, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait and Ha'il

region.text: the southern land Cliopatria's 1873 outline lacks, page silent

ledger.note: 1873: Cliopatria's shape shrinks to Najd and Qassim. 'Saud gained power again in 1873 but died two years later'; about 730 cells of southern desert beyond Hasa leave the shape and no page says why (bridge).

region.text: most of Qassim

ledger.note: 1877: most of Qassim passes to the Rashidis' shape. Page: the Rashidis and Saudis 'engaged into a full scale war over the region of Qassim'; no year is given there, so 1877 is Cliopatria's. The Saudis regain Qassim in 1906 (third-saudi-state).

region.text: the land Cliopatria's 1885 outline lacks, page silent

ledger.note: 1885: a further fringe leaves the Saudi shape (about 220 cells, in Cliopatria's drawing); the pages opened date none of Muhammad bin Rashid's advances before 1887.

region.text: Riyadh and Najd under a Rashidi governor

ledger.note: 1887: Muhammad bin Rashid annexes Najd. Page: 'In 1887 he annexed Najd'; he captured Riyadh and put in a Rashidi governor, Salim Al Sibhan, 'rather than restoring Abdullah bin Faisal'. The Mulayda page gives no date for the takeover and has the Rashidis 'planning' to conquer Qassim and Riyadh before 1891, so the two pages differ.

region.text: the land Cliopatria's 1890 outline lacks, page silent

ledger.note: 1890: the shape falls to about 114,000 km2 in Cliopatria's drawing (the Riyadh and Hasa fringes); no page dates it.

region.text: the last Saudi outline

ledger.note: January 1891: the nominal Ottoman suzerainty lapses with the state. No page gives an end to the relation recognised by Faisal in 1843; recorded as ending with the state.

region.text: the last Saudi outline

ledger.note: January 1891: the Rashidi occupation turns into annexation. After Mulayda the Rashidis 'captured Riyadh and ruled Najd' (Jabal Shammar page).

region.text: the last Saudi outline, passing to Jabal Shammar

ledger.note: 21 January 1891: the Second Saudi State ends at Mulayda. Page: the battle 'occurred on 21 January 1891', 'Decisive Rashidi victory', 'End of the Second Saudi State'; the Rashidis forced the House of Saud, 'led by Abdul Rahman bin Faisal', to flee (the Nejd page: expelled from Najd in 1891).

wars.name: Expedition to Najd (1836)
wars.outcome: Egyptian victory then withdrawal: Mehmet Ali occupied Najd, al-Hasa and Qatif, Faisal was defeated and taken to Cairo in 1838, and most of the army was recalled in April 1840.
wars.note: Egypt also gained 'the submission of Bahrain, Qatar, and Trucial Oman' (undated on the page).

wars.name: Battle of Mesaimeer
wars.outcome: Saudi victory on 2-4 June 1851 near Mesaimeer; Faisal held Qatar briefly and the 25 July peace returned Al Bidda Fort against 4,000 German krones a year as zakat.

wars.name: Saudi war of succession (Abdullah and Saud)
wars.outcome: Saud defeated at Mutala 1866-67, Abdullah fled Riyadh and Saud proclaimed himself Imam in May 1871; Saud ruled again 1873-75; the infighting among Faisal's four sons 'eventually destroyed the state'. No territory changed hands on the page apart from the Ottoman seizure of al-Hasa.

wars.name: Ottoman occupation of al-Hasa
wars.outcome: The Ottomans took al-Hasa in 1871 (Midhat Pasha) and held it until the Saudis took it back in 1913.

wars.name: Faisal's attacks on Bahrain, Oman and the Trucial States
wars.outcome: No gains: three failed tries at Bahrain (1847, 1851 and a later one), failure to take Oman in the 1850s and attacks on the Trucial States in the 1860s that 'the British forces militarily stopped'.

wars.name: Battle of Mulayda

zones.text: Najd and Riyadh, annexed by the Rashidis

wars.outcome: Decisive Rashidi victory on 21 January 1891, the 'last major battle during the period of the Second Saudi State'; the Al Saud fled.
wars.note: Muhammad bin Rashid had annexed Najd in 1887 (his page); the Mulayda page gives no earlier date.

certainty.note: Every frontier of the Najdi emirate is a tribal or desert limit with no survey: Qassim and Ha'il are nominal at times, the Gulf coast is tribute rather than territory, and the Hasa and Rub' al Khali limits are approximate. No treaty fixes a boundary in these years.

sources.title: Emirate of Nejd
sources.note: Identity, founding in 1824, Riyadh, the Egyptian return of 1836-1840, Faisal's Bahrain and Qatar tries (1847, 1851), the Battle of Mulayda and the end in 1891. The infobox came through without its area, capital names or predecessor fields.

sources.title: Faisal bin Turki bin Abdullah Al Saud
sources.note: Faisal's two reigns, Ottoman suzerainty and tribute, Bahrain, Qatar, Oman, the Trucial States, Ha'il (1835 appointment of Abdullah bin Rashid), Hasa operations in 1830, the sons' war.

sources.title: Expedition to Najd (1836)
sources.note: The Egyptian landing of 1836, Khalid in Riyadh in 1837, the occupation of Najd, al-Hasa and Qatif, the April 1840 recall, and Turki's conquests (Arid, Kharj, Mahmal, Sudayr, Aflaj; Hasa by 1830).

sources.title: Saud bin Faisal bin Turki Al Saud
sources.note: Mutala 1866-67, Saud as Imam in May 1871 and 1873-75, Midhat Pasha in al-Hasa. The first fetch of 'Saud bin Faisal Al Saud' returned the 20th-century foreign minister and was not used.

sources.title: Battle of Mulayda
sources.note: 21 January 1891 and the end of the Second Saudi State; the page gives no earlier dates and no Ottoman role.

sources.title: Emirate of Jabal Shammar
sources.note: Ha'il as a vassal 1836-1848 and sovereign 1848-1921; the Qassim war; the 1891 ousting of the Saudis.

sources.title: Unification of Saudi Arabia
sources.note: The Ottoman garrison in al-Hasa from 1871; Riyadh retaken in January 1902 (for the successor state).

sources.title: Muhammad bin Abdullah Al Rashid
sources.note: The Rashidi annexation of Najd in 1887 and the Rashidi governor of Riyadh.

notes:
Split of Cliopatria's row 'Emirate of Nejd' (1824..1925): this dossier is the Second Saudi State, 1824-21 January 1891, and reviews the shapes to 1895 (the 52 km2 sliver of 1895-1904 is marked wrong). The shapes from 1905 to 1925 are the Third Saudi State (Emirate of Riyadh, Emirate of Nejd and Hasa, Sultanate of Nejd), which has its own dossier third-saudi-state (new slug); Cliopatria shapes emirate-of-nejd_1905 to _1924 therefore show as 'no verdict' warnings here and are reviewed there. Dossiers by other groups (asir, kingdom-of-hejaz) name emirate-of-nejd as the conqueror of 1920-1925; those counterparts should read third-saudi-state.

Pages: the Emirate of Nejd article reached me through an extractor that dropped its infobox (no area, no capital names, no predecessor fields, capital years 1824-1834 and 1889-1891 only), so no infobox area was compared. The page budget (9) allowed Nejd, Faisal, the Expedition to Najd, Saud bin Faisal, Mulayda, Muhammad bin Abdullah Al Rashid and, shared with the Jabal Shammar dossier, the Jabal Shammar and Unification pages.

Unsettled: (1) the 1853 doubling of the Cliopatria shape (about +495,000 km2 after removing the Gulf coast) is not dated or described by any page; (2) the Rashidi takeover of Riyadh is 1887 on the Muhammad bin Abdullah page, 1891 on the Mulayda page, and the Jabal Shammar page prints 'occupied the Saudi capital of Riyadh in 1865' in one place and 1891 in another; the ledger follows 1887 (annexation, hatched) and 1891 (end); (3) the Ottoman suzerainty of 1843 is nominal and its end is unknown; it is recorded as a vassal pair only because Rule 4 asks for tributaries, and a renderer may prefer to ignore it; (4) the tribute of Muscat (Faisal page) is undated and has no event; (5) rulers: the pages give only Turki 1824-1834, Faisal 1834-1838 and 1843-1865, Saud 1871 and 1873-1875, so no ruler strip is given.

Counterparts needing care: muhammad-ali-dynasty (the Egyptian occupation), house-of-khalifa (Bahrain and Qatar 1847-1865), qatar-dynasty (the Al Thani of Qatar, a party at Mesaimeer), ottoman-empire (Hasa 1871-1913). Region names the gazetteer lacks: none (Al-Ahsa, Nejd, Trucial Coast and the admin-1 units resolve).
